product_overview: Dynamic AI is an advanced natural language to SQL generation system that leverages Google Gemini LLM and Qdrant vector search to enable users to query complex databases using everyday language. It integrates multi-layered semantic context, intelligent query condensing, caching, and a feedback-driven training dataset pipeline to provide accurate, reliable, and efficient SQL query generation with enterprise-grade safeguards and observability.
core_goals: Enable users to query database systems using natural language without requiring SQL knowledge.
Provide high accuracy in SQL generation through multi-layer context awareness and strict schema validation.
Implement semantic caching and query condensing to optimize response times and reduce redundant processing.
Ensure system safety and prevent hallucinations or malicious SQL execution through layered validation and security checks.
Establish a feedback loop that collects user approval data to refine AI models and support continuous learning.
Offer comprehensive observability including performance metrics, cost tracking, and user satisfaction insights.
Support scalability and maintainability with a clean architecture and modular pipeline design.
key_features: 7-Layer Query Pipeline incorporating Intent Routing, Query Condenser, Semantic Cache, RAG Context, SQL Generation, SQL Validation, and Execution layers.
Intent Router Layer 0: Semantic intent classification with self-learning and auto-seeding via vector search and fallback LLM.
Query Condenser Layer 0.5: Smart handling of follow-up and context-related queries using ActionType modes (NEW, WRAP_PREVIOUS, REGENERATE).
Semantic caching with similarity thresholding and TTL to accelerate frequent queries via Qdrant vector DB.
Multi-layered anti-hallucination defense system including grounding, schema constraints, AST-based SQL validation, and sandboxed execution with rollback on failure.
User feedback system with Like/Dislike controls, context rollback on dislike, and Golden Dataset export for training.
Comprehensive observability backend with real-time dashboard for latency, error rates, cost, and user satisfaction metrics.
Modern Angular frontend with chat interface, data visualization, SQL copying, and real-time metrics display.
Checkpoint-resilient Schema Generator Pipeline for incremental schema ingestion and CDC change detection.
Docker support with configured CORS and static file serving for easy deployment.
user_flow_summary: User submits a natural language question through the Angular-based conversational UI.
Intent Router (Layer 0) classifies the query intent using Qdrant and LLM fallback to route appropriately.
Query Condenser (Layer 0.5) processes follow-up questions and decides on ActionType to optimize SQL generation.
Semantic Cache checks for similar previous queries to return cached SQL if available, skipping redundant LLM calls.
Relevant schema context is retrieved using RAG layer querying Qdrant for semantic schema embeddings.
SQL Generation Service constructs SQL queries guided by strict schema mapping and action type.
SQL Validator analyzes and validates generated queries for security and syntax compliance, blocking harmful operations.
Approved queries are executed in a sandboxed, read-only environment with results returned to the UI.
User reviews the results and can provide feedback through Like/Dislike buttons, triggering context rollback if disliked.
Performance, cost, and user feedback data are aggregated and exposed via Metrics API, powering a live dashboard.
Collected feedback is stored as training examples to maintain the Golden Dataset for fine-tuning future AI iterations.
validation_criteria: Natural language questions produce accurate, syntactically valid, and safe SQL queries conforming to schema constraints.
Follow-up queries correctly condense and preserve conversational context with appropriate ActionType usage.
Semantic caching returns cached query results for semantically similar questions within the TTL period, improving response time.
SQL validator must detect and block any DML/DDL attempts or suspicious query patterns before execution.
System metrics such as latency, token costs, and user satisfaction scores reflect real-time operational status and meet defined SLAs.
User feedback actions correctly update the training example database and allow context rollback on dislike events.
The intent classification service demonstrates high accuracy in routing user queries and self-learns from new intents.
UI components including chat interface, SQL display, and dashboard render and behave responsively across supported browsers.
All security policies including sandboxed read-only query execution and prompt hardening are enforced reliably.
Unit and integration test suites must cover critical services including QueryOrchestrator, SqlGenerationService, QueryCondenserService, and SqlValidatorService with high pass rates.
